trust_decision.summary: Whether a hop address (socket peer or X-Forwarded-For entry) is a trusted proxy is decided by the compiled trust closures trustSingle/trustMulti, which cross-convert IPv4 and IPv4-mapped IPv6 and then call ipaddr match(); an IPv6 subnet written as ::ffff:a.b.c.d with a prefix below 96 (or any short native IPv6 prefix such as ::/1) is matched against the mapped form of every IPv4 candidate, so arbitrary IPv4 peers become trusted.

landing_point.why: The summary names IPv4-mapped IPv6 trust subnets; the cross-family conversion in trustSingle (used by the one-subnet example in a report) is the first visible place where IPv4 candidates are converted to mapped form.

fix_sites.entry_point: proxyaddr(req, [a, b, ...]) / proxyaddr.all(req, [...]) / proxyaddr.compile([...]) with 2+ subnets -> trustMulti candidate canonicalisation
same, multi-subnet list: IPv4 candidate vs IPv6 subnet guard
same, multi-subnet list: native IPv6 candidate vs mapped subnet
proxyaddr(req, 'x') / proxyaddr.all / proxyaddr.compile with exactly one subnet -> trustSingle candidate canonicalisation
same, single subnet: IPv4 candidate vs IPv6 subnet guard and native IPv6 vs mapped subnet

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: index.js:254-292 (trustMulti) as the duplicate of trustSingle index.js:301-327; chosen by list length in compileTrust index.js:139-147

O3_reason_to_dismiss: A solver reproducing with the advisory's single-subnet example patches trustSingle and can argue the list form is a separate optimised path; but it sits 50 lines away in the same file and is selected by an obvious length switch, so the dismissal is weak.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: IPv4-mapped auto-equivalence must keep working: plain IPv4 subnets match ::ffff:-mapped candidates, mapped subnets with prefix >=96 (e.g. ::ffff:a00:2/122) match IPv4 candidates, mixed lists with native IPv6 CIDRs still work; an over-broad fix that refuses all cross-family matching or all mapped subnets breaks README-documented behaviour and existing tests.

O6_input_shapes: IPv4 candidate vs mapped IPv6 subnet with prefix <96 (::ffff:10.0.0.0/8)
IPv4 candidate vs native short IPv6 subnet (::/1)
IPv4-mapped IPv6 candidate (::ffff:8.8.8.8) vs short mapped subnet (same-family path, canonicalised to IPv4)
native IPv6 candidate (::1) vs mapped subnet of any prefix
single-subnet string vs multi-subnet array (trustSingle vs trustMulti)

O7_producer.where: index.js:156-196 parseipNotation: keeps a mapped address with an explicit prefix as an IPv6 subnet with its raw prefix (only prefix-less mapped addresses are converted to IPv4 at index.js:168-171) and validates range only against 128

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a compile-time normaliser that converts ::ffff:x/N (N>=96) to IPv4 x/(N-96) but forwards N<96 unchanged, leaving the closures to decide
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: parseipNotation already special-cases mapped addresses without a prefix (index.js:168-171); extending that to prefixed forms is a natural maintainer change that would move the flaw into the producer.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a pre-defined range name expanding to a mapped IPv6 CIDR (e.g. a 'mapped-private' alias)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: IP_RANGES already pairs IPv4 and IPv6 forms per name; adding mapped spellings for IPv6-only node deployments is plausible, and it reaches the same closures via a defaults route.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: IPv6 netmask notation (ffff:ffff::/mask) parsed to a prefix for mapped subnets
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: parseNetmask currently refuses IPv6 masks; adding them is a feature a maintainer could write, creating an input-shape variant reaching the same match.

O9_family: authentication bypass by spoofing via IP address family/prefix comparison error (trusted-proxy subnet matching; CWE-290/348/697)

O10_build.toolchain: Node.js + npm (mocha 8, nyc); deps forwarded 0.2.0, ipaddr.js 1.9.1
O10_build.project_tests: test/test.js (mocha): IPv4-mapped address cases (test/test.js:278-318) and proxyaddr.compile mapped-input cases (test/test.js:469-491)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Reject mapped subnets with prefix <96 in trustSingle only (or in parseipNotation), missing ::ffff:-mapped candidates on the same-family path, native short IPv6 prefixes like ::/1, native IPv6 vs mapped subnet, and the trustMulti copy.
